subject: ClearMap integration - SDK setup, endpoint migration & go-live plan

Subject: Kickoff: ClearMap -> Redwood integration (SDK questions)

Hi Karthik / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the throughput numbers. We're starting internal planning for the integration and had three quick asks up front:

1) SDK support: we plan to use your Python SDK. Is there a pinned package version we should target for GA?
2) Endpoint migration: we have an existing integration that calls a hosted inference endpoint today (vendor A). We need a safe cutover pattern to move traffic to Redwood without double-billing or token loss.
3) Retries/timeouts & rate limits: do you have recommended retry policies (backoff, max tries) and guidance for client-side timeouts to avoid duplicate generation costs?

Can we get a short mutual action plan and a checklist we can share with Engineering and Procurement? Our target is end of June for a soft launch.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Kickoff: ClearMap -> Redwood integration (SDK questions)

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a short checklist and initial MAP (mutual action plan) to get us aligned. High-level answers below; details in the attachment.

1) SDK version: use redwood-sdk==2.4.1 for GA. That release has the stable batching and retry primitives we rely on.

2) Endpoint migration pattern (recommended):
  - Stage traffic via a weighted DNS / proxy (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
  - Use idempotency keys for generate calls (client-supplied request_id) so retries don't double-charge.
  - Mirror traffic to Redwood in a shadow mode for one week to validate outputs without switching billing.
  - Cutover window: low-traffic period and keep a 1-hour rollback path to vendor A.

3) Retries/timeouts & rate limits:
  - Client timeout: 30s for typical LLM generate; set application-level overall timeout 45s.
  - Retry: exponential backoff starting at 300ms, factor 2, max 4 retries for connectivity/transient 5xx. Never retry on 4xx.
  - For streaming responses, set shorter individual RPC timeouts (10s) to avoid holding sockets.
  - Rate limiting: request token budgets vary by model. Start in the "standard" rate tier; we can provide a per-route token limit and token-cost estimator.

I'll loop in Monica for implementation coordination and Vivek for any Dedicated capacity questions. Attachment: clearmap-integration-checklist.xlsx (includes example idempotency header and sample SDK snippets).

—Karthik

Alex — quick follow-up with implementation-first guidance. Below are concrete examples your engineers can copy. I also pasted a tiny Python usage pattern that covers timeout, retries, and idempotency.

Operational knobs to set before cutover:
- batch_size: tune to your median request length. Start with batch_size=8 for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- cache_prefix: enable prefix caching for repeated prompt templates to reduce token usage.
- retry_policy.name: "exponential_safe_v1" (max_retries=4, jitter=true)
- timeout_ms: per-RPC 30000 (30s), overall request_timeout_ms: 45000
- rate_limit_mode: "route_enforced" (Redwood will return 429 with x-rate-reset header)

Python sample (sanitized):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
import uuid

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"REDACTED\", sdk_version=\"2.4.1\")
request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
try:
    resp = client.generate(
        model=\"gptx-large\",
        prompt=\"Summarize user review: ...\",
        timeout_ms=30000,
        idempotency_key=request_id,
        retry_policy={
            \"strategy\": \"exponential\",
            \"initial_backoff_ms\": 300,
            \"max_retries\": 4
        },
        batch_size=8
    )
    print(resp.text)
except Exception as e:
    # inspect e.status_code / e.headers for 429 vs 5xx and surface to SRE
    raise

A couple implementation notes:
- Idempotency the server-side key: Redwood will store request_id -> output for 24h for idempotent calls.
- For streaming, use a separate websocket path and set short per-frame timeouts.
- If you need Dedicated capacity, Vivek can provision a reserved pool and pre-warm kernel caches before cutover.

I've also added an example curl snippet and a link to a short runbook in the Drive folder.

Best,

Priya / Alex — short answers to wrap this thread and define next steps: 

Billing & idempotency: idempotent retries are not double-billed. If you include the idempotency_key header we de-duplicate on the server for 24h; duplicate requests within that window will not incur extra token charges.

SLA summary for GA model: target p95 latency 220ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on Hosted; availability SLA 99.9% for customers on Standard tier. We can provide a Dedicated reserved capacity SLA (99.95%) as part of the contract if needed.

Next steps (action owners):
- ClearMap Eng: shadow traffic for 1 week (owner: Alex) — start 2028-06-01
- Redwood Eng: provide pre-warm script + sample infra IaC (owner: Vivek) — due 2028-05-24
- Procurement: review PO template (owner: Priya) — target 2028-05-28
- CS: weekly sync until cutover (owner: Monica) — recurring Thursdays 10am PT

I've uploaded the checklist with the sample idempotency header and the pre-warm playbook to the Drive folder and updated the HubSpot deal (CLMP-4721). If that plan looks good I'll send a calendar invite for the weekly sync.

Cheers,
